A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research work, with matching authors, title and retained experiments. All 13 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.1-8B experiments on partial products, arithmetic perturbations, position-level accuracy and input-format robustness.

after.justification: V2 reports original arithmetic fine-tuning results, subgroup-quality analyses and a new comparison of chain-of-thought multiplication strategies.

M1.justification: The analytical procedure changes substantially. V1 defines subgroup quality by maximizing prediction accuracy over possible mappings; v2 replaces this with zero-masking and arithmetic comparison in Algorithm 1, then analyzes subgroups by token budget. Subgroup outputs are also restricted from arbitrary output subsets to individual digits.

E1.justification: Coverage remains within synthetic addition and multiplication, including the existing rule perturbations and 3–5-digit multiplication tasks. V1's natural-language, random-string and disturbed-digit input scenarios in Appendix A.2 disappear, while v2 adds explicit CoT multiplication traces in Section 4.2.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds a comparison of complete standard-multiplication, repetitive-addition, lattice and Egyptian CoT strategies against direct-answer training. These algorithm names already appeared in v1, but there they supplied partial-product diagnostic tasks rather than complete CoT solutions. The original diagnostic comparisons remain in v2 Appendix C.

E3.justification: The stated common training settings change from LoRA rank 64 and model-specific learning rates of 1e-4 and 2e-4 in v1 Appendix A.1 to rank 8 and 3e-4 in v2 Appendix A. V2 also states that hyperparameters were not optimized and adds evaluation of 3-, 5- and 8-step CoT strategies. Twelve epochs and the 8:1:1 split remain; the PDFs do not establish whether retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds subgroup-quality analyses across output positions and token budgets in Figures 4 and 6, plus analysis of entropy and CoT decomposition in Table 3. V1's input-format robustness analysis in Appendix A.2 is removed. The partial-product diagnostics and arithmetic-rule perturbation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional averages concern subgroup metrics and do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Table 3 newly reports accuracies of 73.12% for direct answers, 86.32% for standard multiplication, 91.31% for repetitive addition, 94.41% for lattice and 98.31% for Egyptian CoT. Figures 4 and 6 add subgroup-quality results, while v1's format-perturbation results disappear. The retained partial-product and rule-perturbation accuracy values and position-level curves match across versions; the new CoT scores are not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal Solomonoff-induction, Kolmogorov-complexity and Bayesian-updating definitions, Proposition 1.4, and a token-inclusion monotonicity claim in Equation 4. It revises the subgroup and quality definitions and introduces budget-dependent best quality. V1's multiplicative difficulty hypothesis and Appendix A.3 diagnostic derivations are removed.

C1.justification: The symbolic-learning conclusion and U-shaped accuracy observation remain, but the principal contribution becomes Solomonoff-inspired subgroup induction and a hierarchy of increasingly complex token shortcuts. V2 also claims that subgroup entropy estimates errors and helps explain CoT strategy quality, substantially extending the contribution beyond v1's partial-product and subgroup-complexity account.

C2.justification: V2 develops a tree-search explanation of learning, distinguishes computationally costly quality analysis from cheaper entropy-based error estimation, and interprets CoT gains through decomposition entropy. The CoT omission acknowledged in v1's limitations is addressed, but the explicit limitation concerning natural-language benchmarks such as GSM8K and MATH is dropped.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code link, batch size, checkpointing information, explicit dataset totals and validation-loss checkpoint selection. It omits v1's warm-up, weight-decay, LoRA alpha/dropout and Unsloth/vLLM details. These are limited additions and losses in reproducibility documentation beyond the protocol revisions.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated discussion connecting language models with Solomonoff induction, universal computation and Bayesian learning, citing works including Solomonoff, Ortega et al., Young and Witbrock, and Grau-Moya et al. Earlier mathematical-training and benchmark coverage is compressed. The paper is substantially repositioned around algorithmic learning theory.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and the narrative is reorganized around induction, subgroup quality and entropy. Related work moves toward the end; setup and partial-product material move into appendices. The dedicated Limitations and Ethics sections and the format-perturbation appendix are removed.

P2.justification: The paper switches from two-column to single-column layout and redraws the overview diagram. It adds tree, learning-phase and subgroup-quality figures, Algorithm 1 and a CoT table; adds an entropy column to the perturbation-results table; and removes the format-perturbation tables. Retained diagnostic displays are relocated and enlarged.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's untested CoT extension and adds explicit subgroup analyses and code-access information. However, its new metric-based evidence has unresolved inconsistencies: Table 3 reports average Q(s) values of 4.02–9.87 although Definition 2.2 bounds Q(s) by 1, and Section 4.1 defines H' as summed positional entropy while Table 2 reproduces joint-entropy values. These issues, together with lost implementation details, make it unclear whether the additions outweigh the reduced mathematical and reproducibility clarity.
